newsitem.title: USA: News Corp says U.S. probe looks at coupons.
newsitem.headline: News Corp says U.S. probe looks at coupons.

text.p: News Corp Ltd said the U.S. Department of Justice probe into its proposed acquisition of Heritage Media Corp is focused on the coupon operations of both companies.

News Corp, which announced the proposed acquisition in March, operates a business that provides merchandise coupons in newspapers, as well as a smaller business that provides coupons found in grocery stores.
Heritage also has an in-store coupon operation.
"Our argument is that the market is broader than the way they describe it," said News Corp spokesman James Platt.

Both companies earlier announced the Department of Justice will take additional time to either challenge the transaction or approve the deal. The government already had issued a "second request" for more information that was set to expire later this week, Platt said.
The deal originally was valued at $754 million in stock. The terms also call for News Corp to assume $600 million in Heritage debt.
Shares of Heritage tumbled 2-8/16 to 16-11/16 in afternoon trade on investor concerns about the transaction.
